course_name_original: Seguridad y Legislación en la Gestión de los Datos
course_name_en: Security and Legislation in Data Management
prerequisites: Ability to read and comprehend documentation written in English

learning_outcomes.text: Know the legal framework and constitutional protection related to data engineering.
Know the fundamental aspects of data protection.
Know the basic principles and regulations of computer security.
Understand and apply techniques to provide data confidentiality.
Understand and apply techniques to provide data integrity.
Understand and apply techniques to ensure data authenticity.
Know and understand mechanisms for secure data transmission.
Know and understand authentication techniques and mechanisms.
Know the basic principles of a computer security audit.

syllabus_topics: Fundamental rights and their effectiveness in cyberspace
Legal regime of Data Protection and Electronic Identification
Introduction to Security: Policies, Norms and Security Standards
Confidentiality, Integrity and Authenticity of Data
Protection of Communications and Data Access
Legal regime, legislation, policies and security risks of cyberspace
Constitutional protection of cyberspace. Fundamental rights and their effectiveness in cyberspace
Legal regime of Data Protection and Electronic Identification
Confidentiality, Integrity and Authenticity of Data
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade is calculated as: 0.45 x Theory Part + 0.4 x Practical Part + 0.10 x CV Participation + 0.05 x Attendance. A minimum score of 5 out of 10 is required in each theoretical and practical exam (legislative and computer parts) to pass the subject. If any part is failed, the final grade will be the lowest failing mark. Approved theoretical or practical parts from each domain (Law and Computer Science) are retained for subsequent official calls within the current academic year, but not for future years. For the extraordinary call and differentiated evaluation, the final grade is 0.5 x Theory Part + 0.5 x Practical Part, with a minimum of 5 out of 10 required in each theoretical and practical part (legislative and computer/technological parts).
